title: Multistability and Critical Frustrated Superradiance in Open Anisotropic Quantum Rabi Trimer
authors: Ya-Ping Ni, Yi-Ge Wu, Jie-Qiao Liao, Jin-Feng Huang
abstract: We study the nonequilibrium steady states of an open anisotropic quantum Rabi trimer. Combining semiclassical and quantum mechanical treatments, we map out the system's phase diagram and elucidate the critical phenomena induced by anisotropic light-matter coupling, cavity dissipation, and complex photon hopping, which give rise to abundant multistable phases. Counterintuitively, the frustrated superradiant phase (FSP) can be stabilized by both positive and negative photon hopping, a feature absent in closed Rabi and Dicke trimers. We further uncover two independent dissipation thresholds for the normal superradiant phase and the FSP. Unlike isotropic open quantum Rabi trimers, both phases are suppressed once the dissipation exceeds their respective critical values. The rotating and counter-rotating interaction terms exhibit mutually reciprocal effects on the quantum phase transitions. By analyzing universal scaling behaviors with quantum fluctuations incorporated, we reveal an unprecedented finite-fluctuation critical exponent for the FSP. Moreover, the critical exponents of individual phases are coupling-strength dependent. The multistability and FSP can be tuned by anisotropy and dissipation. Our results broaden the scope of nonequilibrium quantum phase physics in few-body systems and hold promising applications for quantum state engineering and cavity/circuit quantum electrodynamics.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex, non-equilibrium phase diagram of an open anisotropic quantum Rabi trimer. It reveals the existence of multiple stable phases, including a unique frustrated superradiant phase stabilized by dissipation. The findings offer new insights into controlling quantum dynamics in cavity QED systems using anisotropy and dissipation.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonequilibrium steady states and critical phenomena exhibited by an open anisotropic quantum Rabi trimer.
main_result: The system exhibits abundant multistable phases, and the frustrated superradiant phase (FSP) can be stabilized by both positive and negative photon hopping, a unique feature of open systems.
method: The research combines semiclassical mean-field analysis with full quantum mechanical treatments to map out the system's phase diagram.
model_or_system: The model is an open anisotropic quantum Rabi trimer, consisting of three ring-coupled cavity-QED cells, governed by a Lindblad master equation accounting for cavity dissipation.
key_observables: Order parameters include cavity-field coherence and atomic spin polarization; critical exponents ($ eta_n$) characterize quantum phase transitions.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the anisotropy parameter ($\epsilon$), cavity dissipation rate ($\kappa$), and the photon hopping phase ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis contrasts open system dynamics with closed models and incorporates quantum fluctuations beyond semiclassical approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams in the $( ar{\kappa}, \lambda)$ plane showing phase boundaries, and show the dependence of order parameters on anisotropy ($\epsilon$) and dissipation ($\kappa$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the nonequilibrium phase diagram, analyzes the stability of superradiant phases (NSP and FSP) against dissipation, and determines critical exponents by incorporating quantum fluctuations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for AMO physicists as it explores complex, non-equilibrium quantum phase transitions in cavity QED systems, providing tools for quantum state engineering.
